scenario: AITA: My friend sent me a screenshot of her grades, and I'm upset | The other day my friend texted me: "\[cramberrycat\], look, isn't it beautiful?" and sent me a screenshot of her grades: a column of straight A's. It was only this narrow strip, which means she must've taken the pains to crop the screenshot so only the grade letters showed up: no class names, percentages, or extra stuff. ​ I forgot exactly what I did. I know I was kind of surprised and irritated that she did this. (Who sends their friends screenshots of their grades? Is this a thing? If so, please fill me in.) Granted, we are on the nerdier side of friends and of course we talk about grades, but I felt like this was too much. I might've ignored her text for a few hours because I was afraid I might say something wrong, which would probably mark me as the A-hole, but I can't remember if I did. ​ Some time after she had already sent the screenshot, she texted me "Sorry" so I'm not sure, maybe she realized how I might feel and apologized for crossing some sort of line? (If there is, in fact, such a line?) I eventually replied, "Truly a sight to behold", which was deliberate in that it did not reflect my true feelings at all. ​ But in terms of my feelings, and my non-verbal reaction, AITA? Was I wrong to be so upset by it? I just felt it was kind of annoying and unnecessary. I'm not sure if she did it with the intention of hurting me or making me jealous; I'm less open about my grades than she is, because she gets consistent high A's on tests while I get B+'s to low A's, although formerly I was a high A's student. I just feel like I'm being too sensitive or overanalyzing it, which has been the case many a time in the past.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was wrong to be upset when my friend sent me a screenshot of her grades. Let me break this down step by step. First, my friend sent me a screenshot of her grades, which were all straight A's. She cropped it so only the grades showed, no class names or percentages. I was surprised and irritated. I mean, why would someone send their grades to a friend? Is that normal? I don't remember people doing that before, so maybe it's not something that's commonly done. I felt like it was too much. She knows I'm not as open about my grades because I don't get the same high A's she does. I used to be a high A's student, but now I get B+'s to low A's. Maybe she didn't realize how I'd feel about it. She even apologized later, which makes me think she might have crossed a line without intending to. I ignored her texts for a few hours because I was afraid of saying something wrong. Then, when I did reply, I said, "Truly a sight to behold," which wasn't how I really felt. I was trying to keep things cool, but inside, I was upset. Now, I'm wondering if I was overreacting. Maybe it's just me being too sensitive. I don't want to come off as petty, but I also don't want to ignore my feelings. Is it wrong to be upset, or was she just sharing something she was proud of? I guess I need to consider her perspective. She might have been excited about her grades and wanted to share them. But by cropping the screenshot, she might have been trying to show off without giving too much detail. Maybe she didn't think about how it would make me feel. On the other hand, I should also think about why her grades upset me. Am I feeling insecure about my own grades? Maybe I'm comparing myself to her, which isn't healthy. But at the same time, it's okay to feel a bit jealous or upset if someone else's success makes me feel inadequate. I also wonder if there's an unspoken rule about sharing grades. Maybe she didn't realize that it's not something friends typically do. Or maybe she thought it was normal because we talk about grades sometimes. But the way she presented it, cropped and only showing the grades, felt a bit boastful. I should also consider how I reacted. I ignored her for a while, which might have made things worse. Then, when I did reply, I wasn't honest about my feelings. That could lead to more misunderstandings. Maybe I should have talked to her about how her message made me feel instead of bottling it up. In the end, I'm not sure if I was wrong to be upset. It's possible that I was being too sensitive, but it's also valid to feel hurt if someone's actions make me feel inferior. I think the key is to communicate my feelings openly and see if we can understand each other better.
